messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from the auth design sync 1: proposal: attach a compact signed policy-envelope to each credential that encodes explicit runtime constraints (resources, actions, allowed_callers, expiry).

colin: Policy envelopes instead of freeform delegation blobs sounds promising. How is this different from role_bindings + delegation?

maya: The envelope is authoritative and immutable once issued (until explicit transfer). It9s the single source of truth for what that key can do at runtime. Role_bindings remain for RBAC, but runtime first intersects role-derived permissions with the envelope9s allow-set.

riley: Immutable envelope helps with offline verification and audit. How do we sign/verify efficiently?

maya: Sign with a platform signing key. Auth servers keep a hot in-process cache of recent public keys + verified envelopes (TTL 20s). Envelopes are compact (base64 protobuf) and limited to 1-2KB. Verify = one signature check + parse.

colin: What about delegation that needs to narrow permissions (project hands a subset to a service)?

maya: Delegation produces a new envelope signed by the delegating principal9s key. The new envelope must be a subset of the parent envelope. We store a small lineage pointer in the credential row to the parent envelope id. Runtime checks envelope ancestry only when needed (cached).

riley: Revocation model? Bumping a revocation counter on the credential row should invalidate envelopes issued before that generation. Super simple lookup.

maya: Exactly. Also add a short-blocklist blob for emergency kills on the credential (small list of offender envelope ids) so infra can revoke a single delegated envelope without rotating the whole key.

infra-bot: schema-check: add envelope_id, envelope_blob, parent_envelope_id, rev_gen, blocklist_blob. Ensure envelope_id indexed. Online add-column ok.

colin: Migration: for legacy keys create a default envelope that mirrors current role_bindings and mark as inferred. Flag enforcement behind FF and roll.

riley: Perf note: auth path must remain single-row lookup + local cache verification. No network calls. Add metrics for envelope-verify latency and envelope-miss rate.

maya: UX: surface "envelope provenance" in UI with explicit badges (explicit | delegated | inferred). Transfers require owner confirmation or platform admin override.

colin: Sounds good. I'll put this in the RFC along with a sample proto and the envelope subset rules.

maya: Thanks 1 — will follow up on API contract and a tiny perf test.
